text:
A king once chose a young man to carry an important letter to a faraway city. “Ride quickly,” said the king. “The letter must arrive before the end of the week.”

The messenger left at sunrise. On the road, he saw many things that tried to stop him. A beautiful garden invited him to rest. A friendly farmer offered him a delicious meal. A group of travellers asked him to join their party.

“I’m sorry,” said the messenger each time. “I have a duty to do.”

On the fourth day, he met an old man by the road. The old man was lying on the ground, and he looked very ill. “Please help me,” he said weakly. “I need a doctor.”

The messenger stopped. He knew he would be late if he helped. But he couldn’t leave a sick man alone. He carried him to a nearby village and found a doctor.

He arrived at the city a day late. He knelt in front of the king’s friend and gave him the letter. “I’m sorry I’m late,” he said.

The man read it and smiled. “This letter says: ‘Choose the messenger who stops to help a stranger. He is the one I need.’”

Moral: Kindness is more important than speed.

quiz.q: The king told the messenger to ride quickly.
The messenger arrived at the city early.
Why did the messenger stop on the fourth day?
o: To help a sick old man
